answer.evidence: The steam rows 1-16 are decor and are not measured. The main body is the yellow mound in rows 17-29. Its width goes 14, 16, 20, 24, 26, then 28 at rows 22-25, then narrows to 26, 24, 20, 16 at rows 26-29, so it widens and narrows like an ellipse. At column x=16 the dark vent opening fills rows 18-21, and the lit yellow rim rows 17-22 form the top surface (contents visible inside an open container). Below it, rows 23-29 are a darker front flank of about 7 rows. This reads as a top surface with a front face, so three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sulfur vent: a yellow mound with a white smoke puff, about one tile in size. The references are full trees with canopy and trunk, so the kind does not match and the comparison is only partial. The measured facts are 19 visible tones per tile (references 7 and 29), 0% near-flat coverage, and 14% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is mostly tinted but includes some dark neutral pixels. By eye the mound has roughly 3-4 yellow/olive steps and the smoke has 3-4 grey-white steps. The smoke puff has some shading, but the mound is small and fairly smooth, with little grain or clumping. It reads thinner and simpler than the tree references, which have layered leaf clumps and shaded trunks. As a 'big' vent it is too small and sparse next to the references, so a careful artist would not accept it as equally rich. Fail, partly because the object is a different kind from the references and partly because it is shallower.
